title: MPM Lite: Linear Kernels and Integration without Particles
abstract: MPM Lite is a new hybrid Lagrangian/Eulerian method that eliminates the need for particle-based quadrature at solve time. Standard MPM suffers from a performance bottleneck where expensive implicit solves are proportional to particle-per-cell (PPC) counts due to particle-based quadrature and wide-stencil kernels. MPM Lite treats particles primarily as carriers of kinematic state and material history. By conceptualizing the background Cartesian grid as a voxel hexahedral mesh, particle states are resampled onto fixed-location quadrature points (cell centers) using compact linear (Q1) kernels. This makes force assembly and time integration proceed without accessing particles, decoupling solver complexity from particle count. A novel stress transfer and rotation-free stretch reconstruction strategy resamples the extensive Kirchhoff stress and derives an optimization-based incremental potential formulation. MPM Lite achieves 1.88x speedup over explicit MPM and up to 15.9x speedup over implicit MPM on practical elastoplastic materials.
